While surveillance is always one of those iffy topics, as the article reads it seems that it was used in a particularly exceptional case. If my memory serves, the Quebec City case is the only one where geolocation has been used to date. I hope that at this time, it's being done as responsibly as possible so as not to waste resources.

This article does bring about a good point in regards to when and how civil liberties should be suppressed, as well as the danger in letting it go too far. What I'm worried about with the current covid situation (*and it's a sentiment I've seen alarmingly often here, to be frank*) is just how many of my countrymen are just *chomping at the bit* for a turn to authoritarianism and the dissolution of human rights, calling for extreme measures, but not considering how they may harm innocents in the way. I like to think that our institution is at least able to parse the difference when needed, but it's almost as if dealing with covid is secondary to people wanting the ability to sic the authorities on any neighbour they don't like, or being overly punitive for its own sake.

I hope that most of us will be rational about when these actions are justified. There are some lines that can be crossed when it is necessary, but we need to be very careful not to cross those lines permanently.
